subject.title: Synchronous transcript I/O scales with tool-result payload size and can block the event loop the liveness monitor samples

question: Is source inspection enough to sponsor an async/offloaded transcript persistence refactor now, or should maintainers require current-main live proof of event-loop delay and liveness recovery first?
rationale: The remaining path is real in source, but the current live tool-result cap changes the original reproduction and the fix crosses broad session persistence invariants.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open with live-repro status until a current-main run captures event-loop delay and any stale-session classification around a large configured-high tool result.

options.title: Sponsor the refactor now
options.body: Assign an owner to design async/offloaded active transcript persistence and land it with cache, lock, repair, and liveness tests.

options.title: Close as sufficiently mitigated
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide current caps reduce the remaining risk enough that no source-level refactor is planned.

recommendation.title: Require live proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open with live-repro status until a current-main run captures event-loop delay and any stale-session classification around a large configured-high tool result.

likelyOwner.reason: The transcript seam and append-lock history makes this the best available routing candidate for the persistence design/proof choice.
